text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkey's political tension rises as the Islamist-led government attempts to open National Security Council (NSC) decisions to parliamentary debate.
- State Minister Abdullah Gul calls for general elections and says the government does not have to implement the military's decisions.
- State security court at last begins a case against some of those allegedly involved in scandal over relations between the state and gangsters.
- Some 20 MPs, including some ministers, are determined to quit the conservative wing of the coalition.
- Parliament speaker warns the government against debating security council decision in parliament. Similar moves led to the government's downfall in 1971.
- Celebrations marking Women's Day to be held in Ataturk Cultural Center in Istanbul on Saturday.
- Industrial production increased by 0.3 percent in January, 1997 compared to the same period last year.
- The cabinet did not meet on Thursday to discuss the military crisis.
